learn.title: SQL tiers, scalability and data protection
objectives: Choose between the DTU and vCore purchasing models and between the General Purpose, Business Critical and Hyperscale service tiers
Choose serverless or provisioned compute, and use elastic pools for many databases with variable load
Scale Azure SQL Database up and out with read scale-out, Hyperscale replicas, sharding and partitioning
Protect data with TDE, Always Encrypted, dynamic data masking, row-level security and ledger tables
Secure access with Microsoft Entra authentication, private endpoints, auditing and Microsoft Defender for SQL
concepts: General Purpose
The budget default. It uses remote premium storage with about 5 to 10 ms latency, up to 4 TB, and has no readable replica.
Business Critical
Local SSD storage with 1 to 2 ms latency, three secondary replicas, a free read scale-out replica and In-Memory OLTP. It costs much more than General Purpose.
Hyperscale

Storage is separate from compute and grows automatically up to 128 TB. Backups use snapshots, scaling takes minutes, and you can add 0 to 4 HA replicas and up to 30 named replicas. There is no SQL license fee.
Serverless compute
Available in General Purpose and Hyperscale on standard-series hardware. Compute scales between a minimum and a maximum vCore setting and is billed per second. Auto-pause leaves only storage billed.
Elastic pool
Many databases share a set of eDTUs or vCores. It suits databases with low average use and spikes at different times. You can set per-database minimum and maximum limits.
Read scale-out
Connections with ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly go to a read-only replica. It is on by default in Premium, Business Critical and Hyperscale, and is not available in Basic, Standard or General Purpose.
Sharding
Spreads data across many databases by a shard key such as tenant ID. Elastic database tools add a shard map manager, data-dependent routing, split-merge and elastic jobs.
TDE

Encrypts data files, logs and backups at rest, and is on by default with a service-managed key. With a customer-managed key in Key Vault or Managed HSM, losing key access makes the database inaccessible.
Always Encrypted
The client driver encrypts columns, so the database engine and DBAs never see plaintext. Secure enclaves add in-place encryption and rich queries on randomized columns.
Dynamic data masking
Masks values in query results for users without UNMASK permission. It does not encrypt data and is not a security boundary.
Row-level security
Security policies with filter and block predicates limit which rows a user can read or write. SESSION_CONTEXT supports apps that connect through one identity.
Ledger
Hashes changes into a blockchain-like structure that makes tampering evident. Tables are updatable or append-only, and digests go to immutable blob storage or Azure Confidential Ledger.
comparisons: Use DTU for simple, bundled, fixed-price databases. Use vCore when you need hardware choice, serverless, Hyperscale, Azure Hybrid Benefit or reserved capacity.
General Purpose vs Business Critical vs Hyperscale

General Purpose is cheapest. Business Critical gives the lowest latency, In-Memory OLTP and a free readable replica. Hyperscale handles databases over 4 TB, scales fast and gives flexible read replicas.
Serverless vs provisioned vs elastic pool
Serverless suits one database with intermittent use. Provisioned suits steady load that cannot wait for warm-up. An elastic pool suits many databases whose peaks do not overlap.
HA replicas match the primary's size and act as failover targets. Named replicas have their own size, name and logins and are only for reads.
TDE vs Always Encrypted vs dynamic data masking
TDE protects data at rest from people who steal files or backups. Always Encrypted hides data from the engine and DBAs. Masking only hides values in results from non-privileged users.
Updatable ledger tables keep a history table of updates and deletes. Append-only ledger tables block updates and deletes completely, which suits insert-only logs.
traps: Serverless is not available in Business Critical or the DTU model, and Hyperscale's minimum auto-pause delay is 60 minutes, not 15.
Geo-replication, long-term retention and a DNS alias stop a serverless database from auto-pausing.
Read-only replicas lag the primary, so code that must read its own writes immediately should use the primary.
Administrators and users with UNMASK permission always see unmasked data, and ad hoc queries can infer masked values.
Rich queries such as LIKE and range comparisons on Always Encrypted columns need enclave-enabled keys with randomized encryption. Deterministic encryption allows equality only.
Azure Hybrid Benefit is not available for new Hyperscale databases because Hyperscale has no SQL license fee.
revision: Choose Hyperscale for databases over 4 TB, fast scaling or many read replicas.
Choose Business Critical for 1 to 2 ms latency, In-Memory OLTP or a free readable secondary.
Use an elastic pool for many tenant databases with uncorrelated peaks, and move a constantly busy database out of the pool.
Add ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly to reporting connections to offload reads at no extra cost.
Shard by tenant ID with the elastic database client library, and run schema changes across shards with elastic jobs.
A customer-managed TDE key needs a vault with soft delete and purge protection. Keep old key versions to restore older backups.
Combine controls: Always Encrypted for secrets, row-level security for tenant isolation, masking for support staff, auditing and Defender for SQL for detection.
Enforce Microsoft Entra-only authentication and private endpoints with public network access turned off.

questions.on: Recommend a database service tier and compute tier
questions.q: A company wants to size an Azure SQL Database by choosing the number of vCores and the hardware configuration, and to apply its existing SQL Server licenses through Azure Hybrid Benefit. Which purchasing model should you recommend?

The DTU-based purchasing model
The DTU model with the Premium tier
The eDTU-based elastic pool model
questions.e: Only the vCore model lets you choose hardware and compute separately and supports Azure Hybrid Benefit. DTU bundles resources at a fixed price.

questions.e: Serverless bills compute per second and pauses after the auto-pause delay. While paused, only storage is billed.

questions.on: Recommend a solution for database scalability

A geo-replica on the same logical server
questions.e: Named replicas have their own service objective and can sit on another logical server with separate logins, which gives access isolation.

questions.e: Without enclaves, deterministic encryption is the only type that supports equality lookups. Randomized is more secure but cannot be searched on the server.

questions.on: Recommend a solution for data protection

questions.on: Recommend a solution for data protection
questions.q: Evaluate these statements about Always Encrypted with secure enclaves in Azure SQL Database. 1: VBS enclaves need no special hardware. 2: VBS enclaves in Azure SQL Database support attestation with Microsoft Azure Attestation. 3: Intel SGX enclaves need DC-series hardware. Which statements are correct?
opts: Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3
Statements 1 and 2 only
questions.e: VBS enclaves in Azure SQL Database do not support attestation. SGX enclaves run on DC-series and need Microsoft Azure Attestation.

questions.on: Recommend a solution for data protection
questions.q: A database uses TDE with a customer-managed key. An administrator removes the server identity's access to the key vault by mistake. What happens to the database, and what should the design include?
opts: It stays online until the next restart, so schedule restarts
Only new backups fail, so monitor the backup job history
It falls back to the service-managed key, so no action is needed
It becomes inaccessible within minutes, so restrict and monitor vault access changes
questions.e: When the server loses access to the TDE protector, the database denies connections and becomes inaccessible within about 10 minutes.

questions.on: Recommend a database service tier and compute tier
questions.q: A General Purpose serverless database has a 60-minute auto-pause delay and no features that block pausing. Billing shows compute charges every hour, all night. Users are not active at night. What is the most likely cause?
opts: The auto-pause delay is below the 15-minute minimum
Backups taken at night always resume the database
Serverless databases bill compute even when paused
A monitoring tool keeps an open session to the database
questions.e: Open sessions are the most common reason a serverless database does not pause. Auto-pause needs zero sessions and zero user CPU.

Add another read-only replica to the database
